title: Amy Winehouse's birth chart
metaDescription: Amy Winehouse's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.1° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Count only what the day settles, and fire still carries five of the nine placements whose signs are settled. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 21.1° Virgo: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Venus. An earth sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 23.5° Virgo, Venus at 23.2° Leo, Mars at 20.3° Leo. Mercury in an earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Jupiter in the same degree of the zodiac from Uranus, 1.2° off exact. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Neptune sextile Pluto at 1.5°, and the Sun conjunction Mercury at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Virgo at 23.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 4.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 fire, 2 earth, 1 water, 1 air by element and 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. Mercury and Venus were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.3° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
